headline: The MTP draft passes score all 248,320 vocabulary rows to choose one token per drafted position; a draft that scores only a shortlist of rows cannot change any output, because the target verifies every draft with its full FP16 head. A 32,776-row shortlist (the 32,768 most frequent tokens of the lab's own 26M-token text corpus plus the tokenizer's special ids, 13% of the vocabulary) gives 193.03 / 193.30 tok/s at one user against 177.56 / 177.26 for the same image without a shortlist, +8.9%, with every gate 12/12. Acceptance drops (about 3.0 tokens per step against 3.43) and the head savings outweigh it.
method: R294 = R293 + docker/r294-draft-head-shortlist.py: VLLM_XPU_DRAFT_LM_HEAD_SHORTLIST=<file> makes make_xpu_int4_draft_copy build the draft-only INT4 head from the listed rows (per TP shard) and apply() scatter the logits into a full-width -inf row. Shortlists from draft-shortlists/build-shortlist.py (lab text) and build-shortlist-v2.py (system docs, Python and image sources). One card, depth 3, INT4 draft head, CLASSPAD=0 (the published single-user path), strict stage: fresh MTP0 pair (G1), shortlisted depth-3 pair (G2), each against the MTP0 oracle (G3). Chain scripts/run-20260912-qwen35-4b-draft-shortlist-chain.sh.

sl64k.note: every token the lab corpus uses; the top-65536 request saturates at 38,662

slbase.note: same image, no shortlist: the in-image control, equal to the published 177.41 / 177.17

slu45k.note: lab-text list (all 38,662) united with the top 32,768 of the broad corpus

slu92k.note: every token either corpus uses (37% of the vocabulary); acceptance equal to the no-shortlist control

slu92k-ladders.config: one card, depth 3, CLASSPAD=1, c1-c64 ladders, four passes, pass 2+ medians
slu92k-ladders.reading: +7% at one user, +5% at c8, +3.5% at c16, +3% at c64: the head is a smaller share of the step as the batch grows, so the shortlist is mainly a single-user and low-concurrency lever. Identity as without the shortlist. The MTP0 lane (no draft head) is the unaffected control.

coverage_of_generated_text: output_coverage_pct is the share of the 4B's own strict-suite output tokens (r3 mtp3-a, 12 x 512) that lie in the shortlist; the lab corpus is narrower than the model's output (top8192 covers 97% of the corpus but 79% of the output).
reading: The gain rises from 8k (a loss) through 16k (+1%) to 32k (+9%) and is flat to 38.7k; the lab-text lists have no more rows to add. Acceptance under the 32k list is about 12% lower (per-position 0.88/0.64/0.52 against 0.92/0.81/0.71) and the step is cheaper by more than that. A list with better coverage of the model's output should keep more of the acceptance; the union lists (chain 2) test 45k, 67k and 92k rows at 98.9 / 99.5 / 99.8% coverage. Chain 2 (union lists, image R294b): 45k 191.7 / 191.4, 67k 191.9 / 191.6, 92k 191.2 / 191.1, all 12/12. The curve is flat from 32k to 92k rows at +8-9%; what changes along it is how the gain is composed. At 32k a 12% acceptance loss is outweighed by a head that reads 13% of the rows; at 92k acceptance is exactly the control's (0.922 / 0.815 / 0.715 against 0.915 / 0.806 / 0.709) and the whole +7.7% is the head reading 37% of the rows. The 92k list is therefore the one to serve: nothing is lost in drafting, so it is the least sensitive to text the corpora never saw.
acceptance_metric_caveat: 'Mean acceptance length' is the server's last logged running value, not a whole-run statistic; tok/s is the measurement.
recommendation: VLLM_XPU_DRAFT_LM_HEAD_SHORTLIST=/opt/draft-shortlists/shortlist-u-v1all-v2top65k.txt (67,248 rows, 27% of the vocabulary): 191.87 / 191.58 on the 4B (+8.1%) and 124.03 / 124.13 on the 9B (+9.3%), acceptance within noise of the control on both. Lossless by construction and by the gates. A deployment with its own text can rebuild the list with draft-shortlists/build-shortlist-v2.py; a list that misses tokens costs acceptance, never correctness. The 92k list is the fallback for text unlike either corpus (+7.7% with the control's acceptance).
